facts.statement: The extinct bird belongs to the genus Dysmoropelia.
The specific species name is dekarchiskos.
The genus was described by Olson in 1975.
The bird is classified in the family Columbidae.
The bird belongs to the order Columbiformes.
Dysmoropelia is a monotypic genus containing only this single species.
facts.quote: It is monotypic within the genus Dysmoropelia.

facts.statement: The bird was endemic to the island of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean.
facts.quote: It was endemic to the island of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean.

facts.statement: Fossils of the bird date to the Late Pleistocene and were found at the Sugarloaf Hill locality.
facts.quote: It is known from remains of Late Pleistocene (formerly considered to be Middle Pleistocene) age found at the Sugarloaf Hill locality

facts.statement: The bird was fairly large with short wings relative to its body size and robust legs.
facts.quote: It was a fairly large bird with short wings relative to body size and robust legs

facts.statement: The bird was a large dove measuring about 31 cm in length.
facts.quote: Era una paloma de gran tamaño, de unos 31 cm de longitud

facts.statement: The fossils were found in aeolian calcareous sands at the Sugarloaf Hill locality.
facts.quote: It is known from remains of Late Pleistocene (formerly considered to be Middle Pleistocene) age found at the Sugarloaf Hill locality, which consists of aeolian calcareous sands.

facts.statement: The bird is presumed to have been hunted to extinction shortly after the island was discovered in 1502.
facts.quote: It was presumed to have been hunted to extinction soon after the island's discovery in 1502.

facts.statement: Its adaptations are similar to other flightless Columbidae like the dodo and Rodrigues solitaire, though less extreme.
facts.quote: sus adaptaciones son similares a las de otros colúmbidos no voladores como el dodo, la paloma gigante de Viti Levu o el solitario de Rodrigues, aunque menos extremas.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the Greek words dysmoros (unfortunate) and pelia (wild dove).
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego dysmoros (infelices) y pelia (paloma silvestre).

facts.statement: The species name references Napoleon Bonaparte's exile to Saint Helena, deriving from Greek terms meaning 'leader of ten men' and 'small cape'.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del término griego dekarches (literalmente, el líder de 10 hombres), y el diminutivo masculino iskos, que literalmente significa "Pequeño Cabo", en referencia al título de Napoleón Bonaparte, quien fue exiliado a la isla de Santa Elena.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is estimated from 0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Late Pleistocene (0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago)
